member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Analysis.VariableKey
member.summary:
A key used to identity the variable for state assignment or access. It can contain one of three situations:
(1) A valid path for a global scoped variable -> (name, false, true) (2) A valid path for a dialog scoped variable -> (declaringDialog, name) (3) A valid path for a system variable available in all dialogs -> (name, true, true) (4) A valid path for a system variable available in one specific dialog -> (declaring, name, true) (5) Any other path not considered a valid variable (name, false, false)
This is needed in favor of a standard PropertyPath for two reasons: - We key dialog scopes by their actual dialog. For example. Dialog.Foo in dialog A is different from Dialog.Foo in dialog B. - We only care about the first two parts of the path (scope / name). E.g. Dialog.Foo or Global.Bar.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.BotElementDiagnostic.ErrorMessage
member.summary:
The error message is initialized lazily based on the error kind and its properties. For more details, refer to the xml definition file.
Error messages support C#-style string interpolation using property placeholders, e.g., "An error occurred with Kind={Kind} and ErrorCode={ErrorCode}".
During code generation, these expressions are replaced using standard .NET formatting indices such as {0}, {1}, etc., based on the order of the properties.

If valueExpression has a powerfx expression representing an array, this method will return True and a list representing the static string items in that array. Non-static string items will be ignored.
Example: ["a", 15, "c"] will return True and a list containing "a" and "c"
Example: ["a"+"b", "c"] will return True and a list containing just "c"

member.returns: True if expression represents a parseable array else False

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.LocalizedValuePathInfo
member.summary:
Contains information required to track primary key scopes in combination with structural property paths. For example: botcomponent(id).trigger(main).action(question_foo).prompt.text[1] This references the second alternative in the collection linked to a particular question node by id. The identying reference is stable, even if actions are added or removed before or after the content.
Each path has a structural component and a key reference component. The path can be constructed on the fly by appending elements, the structural component of the path will be replaced by a new keyed reference automatically when calling .

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.LocalizedValuePathInfo.Path
member.summary:
The path using primary key segments and path access. For example: botcomponent(id).trigger(main).action(question_foo).Text
This path references a botcomponent, then a trigger, then a dialog action, then the Text property. The path is a stable identifier, even if nodes are added or removed in the middle of the tree.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.LocalizedValuePathInfo.Kinds
member.summary:
The that was found on each path segment that contains a primary key. Example path botcomponent(id).trigger(main).action(question_foo) would contain the following entries:
Note that only concrete types are included here. We should use to check for abstract type matches.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSourceGreen.Temperature
member.summary: Controls randomness. Lowering the temperature means that the model will produce more repetitive and deterministic responses. Increasing the temperature will result in more unexpected or creative responses. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSourceGreen.TopP
member.summary: Similar to temperature, this controls randomness but uses a different method. Lowering Top P will narrow the model's token selection to likelier tokens. Increasing Top P will let the model choose from tokens with both high and low likelihood. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSourceGreen.StopSequence
member.summary: Make the model end its response at a desired point. The model response will end before the specified sequence, so it won't contain the stop sequence text. For ChatGPT, using |im_end| ensures that the model response doesn't generate a follow-up user query. You can include as many as four stop sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSourceGreen.MaxTokens
member.summary: Set a limit on the number of tokens per model response. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. One token is roughly 4 characters for typical English text. If left empty, the model will use its max context length.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.BotSpeechSettingsGreen.InterdigitTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary: This timeout limit applies when your user hasn't met the minimum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. The interdigit timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used. The minimum recommended limit length is 500 ms.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.BotSpeechSettingsGreen.TerminationTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary: This timeout limit applies when the user has met the maximum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. After the limit times out, the bot will accept the input as complete and won't wait for more input. If the termination timeout is turned off, input will immediately be considered complete after it matches the maximum length specification. The termination timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used.

Description: The timeout limit applies when the bot doesn't detect any user input. If no user input is detected within the time limit, the bot can re-engage with the user. Silence detection for telephony begins timing after the IVR finishes speaking.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.BotSpeechSettingsGreen.UtteranceEndTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary:
incomplete_timeout in collectionsettings for nuance.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.ExternalModelConfigurationGreen.Temperature
member.summary: Controls randomness. Lowering the temperature means that the model will produce more repetitive and deterministic responses. Increasing the temperature will result in more unexpected or creative responses. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.ExternalModelConfigurationGreen.TopP
member.summary: Similar to temperature, this controls randomness but uses a different method. Lowering Top P will narrow the model's token selection to likelier tokens. Increasing Top P will let the model choose from tokens with both high and low likelihood. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.ExternalModelConfigurationGreen.StopSequence
member.summary: Make the model end its response at a desired point. The model response will end before the specified sequence, so it won't contain the stop sequence text. For ChatGPT, using |im_end| ensures that the model response doesn't generate a follow-up user query. You can include as many as four stop sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.ExternalModelConfigurationGreen.MaxTokens
member.summary: Set a limit on the number of tokens per model response. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. One token is roughly 4 characters for typical English text. If left empty, the model will use its max context length.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Internal.DtmfTerminationOptionsGreen.TerminationTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary:
If the value is 0, it means return value immediately. term_timeout in dtmf_settings for nuance.
Description: This timeout limit applies when the user has met the maximum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. After the limit times out, the bot will accept the input as complete and won't wait for more input. If the termination timeout is turned off, input will immediately be considered complete after it matches the maximum length specification. The termination timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.PropertyPathCollection.ContainsDescendantProperty(Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.PropertyPath)
member.summary:
If ContainsDescendantProperty returns true, it indicates a descendant path of the input path had been set in the collection.
For example, for the given input property path "A.B", its descendant property paths could be "A.B.C", "A.B.C.D" or more.
This collection: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar, path: Topic.Var => returns true This collection: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar, path: Topic.Var.Foo => returns true This collection: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar, path: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar => returns false This collection: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar, path: Topic.Var1 => returns false

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.PropertyPathCollection.ContainsAncestorProperty(Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.PropertyPath)
member.summary:
If ContainsAncestorProperty returns true, it indicates one of the ancestors of given input path had been set in collection.
For example,for the given input property path "A.B.C", its ancestor property paths could be "A" or "A.B". Given a collection { "A.B" } where "A.B" had been set with value, ContainsAncestorProperty("A.B.C") returns true.
Corner cases: 1. When collection is { "A.B.Z" } where "A.B.Z" as a sibling path of "A.B.C" had been set, ContainsAncestorProperty("A.B.C") returns false. Since there is no direct value set on any ancestor paths of "A.B.C".
2. When collection is { "A.B.C" } where "A.B.C" had been set, ContainsAncestorProperty("A.B.C") returns false. Since "A.B.C" is not an ancestor path of "A.B.C", and none of "A.B.C" ancestor paths had been set in collection.
This collection: Topic.Var (children=0), path: Topic.Var.Foo => returns true This collection: Topic.Var (children=0), path: Topic.Var.Foo.Bar => returns true This collection: Topic.Var (children='Bar'), path: Topic.Var.Foo => returns false This collection: Topic.Var (children='Foo'), path: Topic.Var.Foo => returns false

member.summary: Computes the differences between the original and modified input sequences on the bounded range.
member.returns: An array of the differences between the two input sequences.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Merge.DiffFinder`1.ScanEqualRegion(System.Collections.Generic.List{Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Merge.IDiffChange},System.Collections.Generic.IEqualityComparer{`0},System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Scan a 2-way EQUAL region and create one or more DiffChanges for the sub-spans that have ignorable changes. (Or rather, changes that were ignored by the comparer in the first pass, but are not ignored by the second comparer.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Merge.DiffFinder`1.DiffEx(System.Collections.Generic.IList{`0},System.Collections.Generic.IList{`0},System.Collections.Generic.IEqualityComparer{`0},System.Collections.Generic.IEqualityComparer{`0})
member.summary:
Computes the differences between the given original and modified sequences. This is an extension on the Diff() method. It uses the primary comparer for the initial computation (to compute the vertical alignment of the changes) and then uses the second comparer to scan the 2-way-equal regions for "unimportant" changes. This can be used to ignore-leading-whitespace for vertical alignment purposes during the primary scan and then to respect whitespace for presentation, for example.
Note that for this to have any effect, the secondary comparer must be MORE STRICT than the primary. And because we only receive generic comparer objects (and not the actual set of ignore flags), we cannot protect you here.
If the secondary comparer is null, we behave like the original Diff().
member.param: The diff element comparer for the second pass.
member.returns: The set of differences between the sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSource.Temperature
member.summary: Controls randomness. Lowering the temperature means that the model will produce more repetitive and deterministic responses. Increasing the temperature will result in more unexpected or creative responses. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSource.TopP
member.summary: Similar to temperature, this controls randomness but uses a different method. Lowering Top P will narrow the model's token selection to likelier tokens. Increasing Top P will let the model choose from tokens with both high and low likelihood. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSource.StopSequence
member.summary: Make the model end its response at a desired point. The model response will end before the specified sequence, so it won't contain the stop sequence text. For ChatGPT, using |im_end| ensures that the model response doesn't generate a follow-up user query. You can include as many as four stop sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.AzureOpenAIOnYourDataKnowledgeSource.MaxTokens
member.summary: Set a limit on the number of tokens per model response. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. One token is roughly 4 characters for typical English text. If left empty, the model will use its max context length.

member.summary:
Returns the record data type that contains all known PVA system variables. (Even if the feature flag was disabled for this variable)
It's used during the type inferrence when we build the semantic model.
It's possible that user is using the system variable but he doesn't have access to it (e.g. he is using IsLoggedIn after the authentication was disabled). In this case, if the variable is used in the expression, we will resolve the type of the expression without the error but we will show an error in the expression saying that the variable is unknow.

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Utilities.ObjectPool`1
member.summary:
Generic implementation of object pooling pattern with predefined pool size limit. The main purpose is that limited number of frequently used objects can be kept in the pool for further recycling.
Notes: 1) it is not the goal to keep all returned objects. Pool is not meant for storage. If there is no space in the pool, extra returned objects will be dropped.
2) it is implied that if object was obtained from a pool, the caller will return it back in a relatively short time. Keeping checked out objects for long durations is ok, but reduces usefulness of pooling. Just new up your own.
Not returning objects to the pool in not detrimental to the pool's work, but is a bad practice. Rationale: If there is no intent for reusing the object, do not use pool - just use "new".

member.name: T:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Utilities.ObjectPool`1.Factory

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Utilities.ObjectPool`1.Free(`0)
member.remarks: Search strategy is a simple linear probing which is chosen for it cache-friendliness. Note that Free will try to store recycled objects close to the start thus statistically reducing how far we will typically search in Allocate.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Utilities.ObjectPool`1.ForgetTrackedObject(`0,`0)
member.summary:
Removes an object from leak tracking.
This is called when an object is returned to the pool. It may also be explicitly called if an object allocated from the pool is intentionally not being returned to the pool. This can be of use with pooled arrays if the consumer wants to return a larger array to the pool than was originally allocated.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.Yaml.YamlSerializationContext.UseYamlPassThroughSerializationContext
member.summary:
Under this context: 1. During Dataverse read, the original yaml string is preserved on the BotElement. 2. During Json serialization, BotComponent's Data field is serialized as a Yaml string. 3. During Json deserialization, BotComponent's Data field is deserialized as a Yaml string. 4. During the Yaml serialization, the original Yaml string is used.
Fields that are passed as "Yaml" string instead of Json has the following property in the xml file: cds:SerializedAs="YamlString"

member.summary: Under this context: 1. During Yaml deserialization, the original yaml string is not preserved. 2. During Json serialization, everything will be serialized / deserialized as a json.
member.param: If true, then the exception will be thrown on deserializing of invalid data. As a result, this exception can be surfaced to the user Or components will be marked as "Legacy" (depending on exception). This is the old / legacy behavior. If false, then we will handle gracefully the error in yaml.

member.summary: The Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) header carries user-to-user call control information between systems. In IVR, the SIP UUI header can be used to pass contextual information like a customer ID or an account number to an external system. member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.Temperature
member.summary: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic. We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.TopP
member.summary: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. We generally recommend altering this or `temperature` but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.TopK
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of most probable tokens that the model considers when generating the next part of the text.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.MaxOutputTokens
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of tokens in the generated chat response.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.FrequencyPenalty
member.summary: Gets or sets the penalty for repeated tokens in chat responses proportional to how many times they've appeared.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.PresencePenalty
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that influences the probability of generated tokens appearing based on their existing presence in generated text.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.Seed
member.summary: Gets or sets a seed value used by a service to control the reproducibility of results.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ModelOptions.StopSequences

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.BotSpeechSettings.TerminationTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary: This timeout limit applies when the user has met the maximum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. After the limit times out, the bot will accept the input as complete and won't wait for more input. If the termination timeout is turned off, input will immediately be considered complete after it matches the maximum length specification. The termination timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.BotSpeechSettings.TerminationTimeoutInMillisecondsIsDefaultValue
member.summary: Returns true if 's value is the default value.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ExternalModelConfiguration.ConnectionReference
member.summary: The logical name of connection reference that points to the connector

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ExternalModelConfiguration.Temperature
member.summary: Controls randomness. Lowering the temperature means that the model will produce more repetitive and deterministic responses. Increasing the temperature will result in more unexpected or creative responses. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ExternalModelConfiguration.TopP
member.summary: Similar to temperature, this controls randomness but uses a different method. Lowering Top P will narrow the model's token selection to likelier tokens. Increasing Top P will let the model choose from tokens with both high and low likelihood. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ExternalModelConfiguration.StopSequence
member.summary: Make the model end its response at a desired point. The model response will end before the specified sequence, so it won't contain the stop sequence text. For ChatGPT, using |im_end| ensures that the model response doesn't generate a follow-up user query. You can include as many as four stop sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.ExternalModelConfiguration.MaxTokens
member.summary: Set a limit on the number of tokens per model response. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. One token is roughly 4 characters for typical English text. If left empty, the model will use its max context length.

member.summary: Additional model specific properties. Use this property when you want to pass additional parameters that you know the underlying model can support.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.DtmfTerminationOptions.InterdigitTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary: This timeout limit applies when your user hasn't met the minimum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. The interdigit timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used. The minimum recommended limit length is 500 ms.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.DtmfTerminationOptions.InterdigitTimeoutInMillisecondsIsDefaultValue
member.summary: Returns true if 's value is the default value.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.DtmfTerminationOptions.TerminationTimeoutInMilliseconds
member.summary:
If the value is 0, it means return value immediately. term_timeout in dtmf_settings for nuance.
Description: This timeout limit applies when the user has met the maximum input length. It applies only to multi-digit DTMF input. After the limit times out, the bot will accept the input as complete and won't wait for more input. If the termination timeout is turned off, input will immediately be considered complete after it matches the maximum length specification. The termination timeout must be a positive whole number and no special characters or letters can be used.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.DtmfTerminationOptions.TerminationTimeoutInMillisecondsIsDefaultValue
member.summary: Returns true if 's value is the default value.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.IGptModelCommonConfiguration.Temperature
member.summary: Controls randomness. Lowering the temperature means that the model will produce more repetitive and deterministic responses. Increasing the temperature will result in more unexpected or creative responses. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.IGptModelCommonConfiguration.TopP
member.summary: Similar to temperature, this controls randomness but uses a different method. Lowering Top P will narrow the model's token selection to likelier tokens. Increasing Top P will let the model choose from tokens with both high and low likelihood. Try adjusting temperature or Top P but not both.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.IGptModelCommonConfiguration.StopSequence
member.summary: Make the model end its response at a desired point. The model response will end before the specified sequence, so it won't contain the stop sequence text. For ChatGPT, using |im_end| ensures that the model response doesn't generate a follow-up user query. You can include as many as four stop sequences.

member.name: P:Microsoft.Agents.ObjectModel.IGptModelCommonConfiguration.MaxTokens
member.summary: Set a limit on the number of tokens per model response. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. One token is roughly 4 characters for typical English text. If left empty, the model will use its max context length.

member.summary: Abstract base class for traversing a bot definition tree to collect information about connector actions.
member.remarks: This walker visits all nodes in the bot definition that represent connector actions (nodes with ConnectionReferenceLogicalName or embedded connector properties). Derived classes must implement the GetConnectorActionInfoFor methods to extract the desired information from each connector action node type. The walker accumulates results during traversal and returns them via the GetConnectorActionInfo method.

member.name: T:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializerAttribute
member.summary: Used to indicate to the compiler that a method should be called in its containing module's initializer.
member.remarks:
When one or more valid methods with this attribute are found in a compilation, the compiler will emit a module initializer which calls each of the attributed methods.
Certain requirements are imposed on any method targeted with this attribute: - The method must be `static`. - The method must be an ordinary member method, as opposed to a property accessor, constructor, local function, etc. - The method must be parameterless. - The method must return `void`. - The method must not be generic or be contained in a generic type. - The method's effective accessibility must be `internal` or `public`.
The specification for module initializers in the .NET runtime can be found here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Ecma-335-Augments.md#module-initializer
